data.name: Diwaker
data.gender_notes: Diwaker is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Diwaker is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'Deep' meaning 'a row of lamps' or 'a lamp'. In Hindu mythology, Diwaker is the god of wisdom and knowledge, who is believed to light the path of knowledge for his devotees. He is also associated with the moon and is known as the 'God of Nights'. The name Diwaker carries the meaning “God of wisdom and knowledge” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Diwaker usually hope their child will grow to embody god of wisdom and knowledge and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Diwaker belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of wisdom and knowledge.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Diwaker total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: Diwaker holds significance in Hindu festivals, especially in Diwali, the Hindu festival of lights. He is depicted as carrying a pot of knowledge on one hand and a lamp on the other. During Diwali, people light Diwakas (oil lamps) and decorate their homes with diyas to celebrate the victory of light over darkness and knowledge over ignorance. Diwali is also known as the 'Festival of Lights'; the lamps represent the wisdom and knowledge that Diwaker, the god, gifts to his devotees.
data.spiritual_significance: Diwaker, the god of wisdom and knowledge, is considered an essential deity for seekers of truth and knowledge.
